```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
```

# Plotly

Make a scatterplot of `body_mass_g` vs. `flipper_length_mm` from the `penguins` data set. Use color and shape to specify the `species`.

Once you have a static graphic you're happy with, convert it to an interactive graphic with `ggplotly()`.

- What tooltips are included by default?
- Change the default tooltip to include "Species"
- (If time) use {stringr} so that the tooltip shows "Species: Adelie" instead of just "Adelie"

Then discuss with your neighbor: would an interactive *bar chart* of `species` add anything? When is an interactive version *not* better?

# Leaflet

The three islands in `penguins` and their approximate locations:

```{r}
islands <- tibble(
  island = c("Biscoe", "Dream", "Torgersen"),
  lat = c(-64.80, -64.73, -64.77),
  lng = c(-63.77, -64.23, -64.08)
)
```

Create a leaflet map with a marker for each island and a popup with the island's name.

::: callout-tip
## Hint

`leaflet(islands) |> addTiles() |> addMarkers(lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat, popup = ~island)`
:::

# DT Table

- Create a {DT} table of the `penguins` data set
- Add the option to filter, and make the font size 14pt

# Putting it all together

Download [`22-dashboard-example.qmd`](https://stat220-f26.github.io/files/22-dashboard-example.qmd) and render it (click **Render**; a dashboard opens in the viewer). Then improve the Penguins data explorer:

1. Make all graphs plotly's with appropriate tooltips
2. Replace the data output with your {DT} datatable
3. Include your leaflet map on a new *page*
4. (if time) Add [value boxes](https://quarto.org/docs/dashboards/data-display.html#value-boxes) on the same page as your map that show the number of penguins that live on each island
5. (if time) Change the [theme](https://quarto.org/docs/dashboards/theming.html) of the dashboard
